text:
inc-bot: 🚨 ALERT triggered: SLO burn-rate for endpoint /v1/generate (hosted) exceeded paging threshold. windows: 5m burn=420%, 1h burn=75%. region=us-east, model_variant=redwood-mix-small. alert_id=ALRT-9832. link: https://monitoring.redwood/prod/ALRT-9832

maya: oncall — I'm seeing the alert. digging into traces now.

maya: preliminary: latency spikes with token stalls, customers seeing slow streaming, not complete errors yet. likely partial degradation not total outage.

zack: grabbing this. paging in my rotation. @maya what's the earliest impacted timestamp?

maya: start ~ 1830002000, peaked 1830002400. Affected ~12 active sessions (mostly web clients).

lee: I can help with logs/traces. sending the tail of the live stream now.

inc-bot: Noted: incident acknowledged by zack. Pager set to ACK.

zack: ok quick triage — kernel-level stalls? Checking GPU queue lengths and KVS misses.

lee: logs show repeated 502s upstream from a inference worker pool but controller still returning 200 with delayed chunks.

elaine: product_ops: any paying customers impacted? I see 3 dedicated seats seeing higher latency, two on Dedicated, one on Hosted.

maya: tagging account team. customer impact appears degraded quality of streaming; recommend notification to sales if it persists beyond 30m.

sam: I'm going to open a temporary alert suppression for the noisy 5m burn window — we should avoid paging every spike while we investigate. Will keep 1h alerts intact.

zack: +1 to suppression but only after we confirm this is noisy, not a real blowup. Please document times and reasons.

sam: executing:```/incident suppression create --alert ALRT-9832 --start 1830002600 --duration 30m --reason "investigation: noisy short burn spikes causing excessive pages"```

inc-bot: suppression created (suppression_id=SUP-441). 5m paging suppressed until 1830004400. 1h burn alerts still active.

zack: digging deeper — discovered a regression in KV cache eviction logic; small model rollout earlier today increased prefix cache churn which amplified token generation latency for long contexts. reproducing locally.

lee: if we can temporarily pin traffic to previous model variant in us-east we should reduce customer impact. can we route a small percentage?

maya: routing policy: try canary rollback to redwood-mix-small:v1.2.3 for us-east for 50% traffic. Ops, can you apply?

elaine: I'll coordinate the rollback and customer comms if needed.

sam: rolling traffic now:```opsctl route update --service inference-hosted --region us-east --model redwood-mix-small:v1.2.3 --weight 50% --dry-run=false```

inc-bot: Deploy traffic change detected by deploy-bot. Route change in progress.

maya: monitoring latency metrics and SLO burn windows. if 1h burn drops below paging threshold we can lift suppression earlier.

zack: local repro confirmed; a small patch to KV eviction fixes the long-tail stalls. planning hotfix, will open PR.

zack: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/evict-fix/pull/57 — request quick review from eng-runtime.

lee: reviewed, LGTM. Can we ship a tiny gate that reduces eviction aggressiveness instead of full fix to limit risk?

zack: yes doing staged ship. will run canary on 10% first.

inc-bot: Note: on-call handoff scheduled in 24m. Current oncall zack -> lee. Handoff doc: https://docs.redwood/oncall/handbook#running-incidents

maya: @lee you'll be shadowing but zack will remain incident owner until next rotation.

lee: got it. will monitor for any regression after the rollback.

sam: monitoring shows 5m burn dropped to 120% within 10m, 1h burn stabilized to 48% and trending down. suppression still active.

elaine: good. I'd like to propose follow-ups: 1) refine paging criteria to require concurrent impact on both 5m and 1h windows or sustained token error rate > X, 2) create a dashboard for prefix cache churn and eviction rate, 3) add a multi-window burn alert that uses weighted windows to avoid noisy pages.

maya: agree on follow-ups. add to incident ticket.

sam: creating tracking tasks now: TASK-1129 (alert rule tweak), TASK-1130 (dashboard for cache churn), TASK-1131 (postmortem + SLAs review).

zack: will merge hotfix after canary looks good. ETA 35m.

lee: after hotfix we should re-evaluate paging thresholds: current rule pages on 5m burn > 300% OR 1h burn > 60%. Proposal: page only if (5m>400% AND 1h>60%) OR (token_error_rate > 0.8%). plus require >3 affected customers to reduce single-customer noisy pages.

maya: that sounds reasonable. let's put proposed rule into a PR and test in staging. Include a rollback plan.

elaine: product_ops will draft a short customer-facing note in case this recurs.

inc-bot: UPDATE: hotfix merged to canary and routing rollback completed. System metrics continue improving.

sam: lifting suppression scheduled only after 1h burn below 50% for 30m. will auto-lift if conditions met.

maya: thanks all. final: incident owner zack, follow-ups assigned to sam/lee/zack. We'll run a short postmortem and adjust SLO paging logic.

zack: adding notes to incident ticket and will run through the oncall handoff with lee in 10m.

maya: closing thread here, continue updates in incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
